NC-2025E1-SB2.aiSummary: The bill would pause North Carolina’s motor fuel tax from the day after it becomes law through November 30, 2026, making the tax rate $0 per gallon during that time. It would also move money to hold harmless several state funds and accounts that would have received that tax money. Through December 31, 2026, it would also stop civil and criminal penalties for certain dyed diesel use for farming and agricultural work, and give some approved users a tax break on dyed diesel for highway vehicles.

It shifts some grant funds, including $1.5 million for hyperbaric oxygen therapy for veterans and changes grants for Harnett County and Anson County. NC-2025-HB199.aiSummary: The bill would create a process for towns and cities to remove land from their borders, and for property owners to ask for that change too. It would require public notice, a public hearing, and a report on how the change would affect city money and services; in some cases, local voters in the area could also vote on it. The bill also sets rules for petitions, hearing notices, and what happens to city services after land is removed.

NC-2025-HB328.aiSummary: The bill would set rules for selling, shipping, and having hemp-derived consumable products in North Carolina. It would require licenses, age checks for buyers under 30 in some cases, child-resistant packaging, and testing and labeling rules, and it would bar sales of some products with more than 0.3% delta-9 THC or certain other hemp cannabinoids. It would also add kratom as a Schedule VI controlled substance and set civil fines and possible criminal penalties for some violations.

NC-2025-HB133.aiSummary: This law changes how a deed or other land record is filed when it covers certain land tied to farmland and military protection rules. The person filing the deed must attach the needed affidavit, and the register of deeds is not responsible for checking or enforcing that step. If the affidavit is missing, it does not change notice, lien order, validity, or insurance of the record.

NC-2025-SB1001.aiSummary: The bill would change coastal rules and permits in North Carolina. It would raise the maximum fee for processing a CAMA permit application, which is a coastal area permit, and would update some rules for upland basin water standards and financial assurance. It would also make technical fixes to the upland basin permit law and clarify state agency authority over the coastal reserve.

NC-2025-HB1240.title: Constitutional Amendment/Early Voting.

actions.text: Ref To Com On Rules, Calendar, and Operations of the House

NC-2025-HB1240.aiSummary: The bill would ask voters to approve a change to the North Carolina Constitution that would give people the right to early voting in primary and general elections held in even-numbered years. It would require at least 14 days of early voting, set minimum hours for early voting sites, and let county election boards set sites and staffing. It would also allow same-day voter registration during early voting.
